text:
sam: short heads-up — ACME reported a large throughput regression on hosted inference around 03:00–03:20 UTC. customer sees RPS drop ~3x and many 503s. they sent two sample request ids: req_8a7f1 and req_8a7f2. asking for repro pack: curl, full request ids, token counts, concurrency profile, and prompt set.

claire: copying the customer's note (redacted): "We started seeing timeouts at ~03:05, median latency jumped from 120ms -> 420ms. No config changes on our side. Using redwood.v1 text-gen, 512 tokens max, batching enabled."

sam: can we get the following from the customer before we dig deeper:
- exact request IDs (full request_id strings, not truncated)
- sample prompt set (10-20 prompts that reproduce the slower tail)
- concurrency they ran (clients/threads, per-second send rate)
- an example curl that hits their code path (headers + body) so we can replay locally
- approximate token counts (input tokens, average and max)

claire: they replied with a minimal curl and said they'll send full request ids in a follow-up DM. pasted their curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":512,"stream":false}'
```

sam: perfect — once we have the full ids we should pull traces from the trace store and ask runtime for metrics. marco / priya — can you outline the minimal repro steps we should ask ACME to run and what we will run internally?

marco: suggested repro steps from runtime side:
1) customer: run their normal load with concurrency X (we asked for exact X) and capture 30s window around the issue.
2) customer: provide the promptset (10–50 prompts) and the exact header set they use.
3) we: replay prompts at the same concurrency against a staging pool with same model & batching config. measure p50/p95/p99 and errors.
4) we: capture "/metrics" (prometheus) and runtime debug logs for the replayed window.

marco: for internal replay here's a suggested wrk command and a tiny python harness for input distribution:
```bash
# example using hey/wrk style:
wrk -t8 -c32 -d30s -s post.lua --latency http://staging-infer.local/replica
```
```python
# simple feeder: rotate prompts, send sync requests, log latency
import requests
for prompt in prompts:
  r = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json={...})
  print(r.status_code, r.elapsed.total_seconds())
```

priya: couple more asks:
- get exact token distribution: average input tokens and 95th percentile output tokens — batching behavior depends on sequence length.
- if they used prefix caching / shared sessions, note that (we need session ids).
- request the request-level logs from their side (client timestamps) to align with server traces.
- recommend they run one controlled test with concurrency=32 and another with concurrency=8 so we can see scaling curve.

debug-bot: Automated note: traced request lookup started for ids: req_8a7f1, req_8a7f2. ETA 2m.

claire: customer just DM'd full ids: req_8a7f1_full_2026 and req_8a7f2_full_2026 and attached promptset (10 prompts) + a short recording of their load generator config. uploading to case doc now.

sam: great. next actions:
- claire: please upload the raw curl + promptset to the support case and confirm they included their concurrency number (requests/sec or threads).
- marco: I'll ask you to run the replay on staging once the case doc is updated. record p50/p95/p99 + error rate.
- priya: please queue a trace correlation for the two request ids and check hot-spot CPU / kernel stalls in the 03:00 window.
- i'll send the customer a small repro harness (python + curl) asking them to run 2 controlled runs: concurrency=8 & concurrency=32, duration=30s each, with the provided promptset.

sam: also include this quick diagnostic curl for them to run (it sets a verbose header):
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-Debug: true" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"<one prompt from set>","max_tokens":128}'
```

marco: if we reproduce, next step is to toggle batching off and run again to confirm batching interactions. also try a quantized model variant to rule out kernel selection regressions.

priya: I'll also drop in a checklist for triage: traces, logs, metrics, kernel profiles, P95 latency per-seq-len bucket.

sam: thanks all — I'll wait for the uploaded case materials and then kick off the staging replay. I'll update this thread when I have replay numbers. :thumbsup:
